pages.title: Before your first block
pages.note: Every school is different. Wait for your school's own list, then ask a second-year what they actually used before you buy anything big. You've got this!

items: Stethoscope or diagnostic kit (some schools hand these out)
Laptop or tablet requirements
Anatomy lab rules: scrubs color, shoes, what to bring
Library e-books and question banks you get free
Required vs. just "recommended" textbooks
One device you can mark up lecture slides on
A second monitor for lectures + notes side by side
A chair and desk you can sit at for hours
Headphones for lectures and the library
Anki set up on your computer and phone
Meal prep containers and a water bottle
Shoes you can stand and walk in all day
A solid stethoscope, if your school doesn't give one
Reflex hammer, penlight, tuning fork (cheap is fine)
Old scrubs and shoes just for anatomy lab
Every book on the recommended list
A premium diagnostic kit before you need one
A big stationery haul for pretty notes

pages.title: First-block setup
pages.note: Set these up in week one, before the first exam shows up. Small systems now save so much stress later!

items: One spot at home that's only for studying
A backup spot (library, study room, coffee shop)
Good light and a charger that lives there
Phone out of reach during lecture blocks
Laptop or tablet + chargers
Water bottle and real snacks
Headphones
Stethoscope on clinical skills days
One calendar with every required session and exam
A weekly plan (pick a planning day!)
One folder per course for slides and notes
Daily Anki reviews before new material
Find counseling and wellness services (before you need them)
Find the learning specialist or academic support office
A simple monthly budget for loan money
Groceries + one batch-cook day each week
One thing that isn't medicine, on the calendar

pins.title: The #1 Med School Shopping Tip: Wait for Your School's List
pins.description: Some schools hand out stethoscopes, diagnostic kits or tablets, and many textbooks are free as library e-books. Check what your school provides and ask a second-year what they actually used before you spend a cent! Free first-year checklist in the post.

pins.headline: Buy mid, not fancy
pins.sub: A solid stethoscope, a cheap reflex hammer, and wait on the pricey diagnostic kit
pins.title: Med School Clinical Gear for First Year: What to Buy and What to Skip
pins.description: For preclinical years, a solid mid-range stethoscope (if your school doesn't give you one), an inexpensive reflex hammer, penlight and tuning fork, and old scrubs for anatomy lab are plenty. Ask an upperclassman before buying a pricey diagnostic kit!
